definition: A Rust Mapping is a pure native projection from explicit borrowed inputs to owned declared fields. It does not construct an Entity, execute invariants, read storage or invoke a Calculation.
internal_result: A v2 Mapping returns a mapping-specific projection struct, including only authored target fields. This keeps partial projections distinct from canonical Entity or Value Object construction.
public_result: A total v3 Mapping to an Interface contract returns that Interface's native public contract struct. Other v3 targets return a mapping-specific projection struct. Public contract identity is never flattened into a domain record.
expressions: Typed literal, path, variant and to_set expressions are lowered statically. Optional defaults are lazy. Values are cloned only when crossing the explicit owned result boundary and retain their qualified native type.
module: One collision-free module per qualified selector under src/application/mappings. Interface and domain imports are derived from checked bindings.
verification: Deterministic planning, Cargo execution for internal and public projections, no hidden Calculation symbol, exact output typing and wrong-result compile-fail controls are required.
compatibility: Legacy v1 raw-property absence semantics remain on their existing paths; no coercive Rust migration is invented. Existing schemas and generators remain unchanged and this candidate has no default cutover.
